runtime.execution: Compiled Tokio service handlers and typed client/context futures around external protocol VM; optional tunneled endpoint transport.
runtime.service_boundary: Consumes Restate server/durable state and external effect services; SDK hosts a service endpoint, not an agent/model loop or service governor.

summary: Rust typed service/object/workflow, journaled closure, durable call/wait and ingress APIs

inspection.scope: context traits/retry rules, RunFuture state machine, durable error interception and real fake-server ingress/tunnel lifecycle tests
inspection.limits: Shared-core/server settlement and full fleet recovery studied separately. No compiled reference or tests ran.

actions.name: #[service]/#[object]/#[workflow] + #[handler]; Endpoint.bind
actions.output: Service endpoint and typed generated clients
actions.lifecycle: Compiled deployment; durable runtime separate; object serial/exclusive key contract
actions.authority: Developer/service process; no model modification/approval loop

actions.name: ctx.run(closure).name(...).retry_policy(...).await
actions.input: FnOnce async closure with serialized output and retry policy
actions.lifecycle: VM ExecuteRun→closure→propose completion→await; immediate-await restriction; no external atomicity guarantee
actions.authority: Service caller code/credentials; context operations forbidden inside run

actions.name: service_client/object_client/workflow_client request.call/send
actions.output: Durable result future or invocation/send identity
actions.lifecycle: Server records/schedules retries; virtual-object waits can deadlock cycles
actions.authority: Caller/server routing; server owns durable work

actions.name: ctx.signal / invocation_handle(id).signal(name).resolve
actions.lifecycle: Survives host attempt via server; not a bidirectional peer room

actions.name: IngressClient.call/send and invocation_handle
actions.output: Decoded result plus invocation ID/follow-up handle
actions.lifecycle: Request transport is replaceable; server work identity distinct from local client

actions.name: Tunnel drain/overlapping replacement and close
actions.output: Replacement session and reaped old/new drivers
actions.lifecycle: Connection handover; not application executable rebuild or unresolved-effect settlement

actions.name: ctx.get/get_keys/set/clear/clear_all
actions.lifecycle: Object state across invocations; workflow state per run; attempts rebuild locals
actions.authority: Context type constrains readable/writable scope; server owns storage

evidence.claim: Run future executes closure only on VM ExecuteRun, proposes serialized result then waits VM result; cancellation branch explicit.
Journaled result contract, no nested context use in run, and immediate-await restriction to avoid replay nondeterminism.
Named run/retry options; actual attempts/duration may exceed configured because closure executes before server receives result.
Typed service/object/workflow call keys, idempotency scope and server-owned journal/retry contract.
Virtual-object serial ordering and explicit cyclic deadlock limits.
Named signal targets invocation ID/name; one-shot durable promise, composable select.
VM/internal future error marks context failed and returns Pending for handler state interception.
Typed ingress client call and returned invocation handle contract.
Fake Cloud HTTP2 session verifies distinct IDs/drain protocol and owned socket/driver task completion.
Capture fake transport records exact requests and queued responses; no live server dependency in this oracle.
Typed get/get_keys/set/clear traits forward to context; only objects/workflows carry writable KV scope.

tests.oracle: Fake Cloud sessions require drain acceptance/distinct IDs and await owned driver completion within timeout; transport liveness, not harness rebuild.

tests.focus: Typed ingress wire requests and retained responses
tests.oracle: Deterministic capture transport permits literal route/header/body/error oracles; server durability/external side effects remain separate.

strengths: Explicit state machine separates closure execution, result proposal and replay wait.
Typed invocation identity and direct fake transport/drain lifecycle oracles.
limits: External side effect and journal completion are not one atomic transaction.
Immediate-await restriction and serial object cycles limit composition; connection handover is not self-refit.
arconaut_questions: How should replay compatibility and side-effect settlement be represented when replacing a compiled workflow program?
Can service/tunnel identity remain independent of a refitting consumer while all that consumer’s active work is accounted for?
